# zen-proxy — full documentation

> Everything from the project README, in one plain-markdown file for LLMs.

Source: https://github.com/12errh/zen-proxy

---

a local proxy that unlocks opencode's anonymous free models for any agent — over both the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs.

anonymous free tier  ◦  no accounts  ◦  no keys  ◦  openai + anthropic compatible  ◦  claude code  ◦  100% local

> **Zen Proxy** is a zero-dependency, locally-run proxy that unlocks opencode's Zen free tier **for any coding agent — not just opencode**. It speaks two wire formats: the OpenAI API, and the Anthropic Messages API so **Claude Code** can use the free models directly, tools included.
>
> opencode gives you free models like `mimo-v2.5-free`, `big-pickle`, and `nemotron` — but only to requests that look like they come from opencode itself: the right `User-Agent` **and** a complete session identity (`x-opencode-session` *and* `x-opencode-session-id`). Most agents force their own identity and get shut out with `400 MissingSessionID` or `403 FreeTierError` ("OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"). Zen Proxy quietly speaks for them: it injects the correct `User-Agent`, mints stable per-client session IDs, forwards your real IP, and re-exposes everything as a standard `/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/models` API.
>
> The result: whatever tool you love — Cline, Roo Code, Continue, Aider, mimo, or a plain `curl` — can now ride opencode's free models with **zero accounts, zero API keys**, and zero config beyond a `baseURL`.

**What it enables:**

- **Free models outside opencode, over either API** — OpenAI-compatible agents *and* Claude Code, keep the free tier
- **Anonymous access with no accounts or keys** (`Bearer public`), or bring your own Zen key (BYOK) for your own quota
- **Smart model fallback** — when one free model is saturated, it rolls to the next
- **Model aliases** — call them `gpt-4o` or `claude-3-5`, get routed to free models
- **Self-updating** — tracks new opencode releases (auto User-Agent) and a GitHub Action keeps the shipped free-model list current as models come and go
- **Per-IP fairness** — real client IPs are forwarded (local clients fall back to the machine's real IP)
- **A retro-zine management dashboard** — stats, one-click model tests, live config, and logs at `http://127.0.0.1:8787/`
- **One-file install** on Linux, macOS, and Windows with a single `curl`

---

## why it exists

opencode's free `-free` models (`mimo-v2.5-free`, `big-pickle`, `nemotron`, …) are only served to requests that mimic the real client. Since opencode started requiring a full session identity, anything missing it gets `400 MissingSessionID`, and anything carrying only half of it gets `403 FreeTierError: "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"` — even with a valid API key. The gateway is served from `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1`; the older `/zen/v1` base still lists models but now rejects all agent traffic. Most coding agents — like the *mimo* CLI fork — force their own identity and get slammed with that error (or `429 FreeUsageLimitError`).

**zen-proxy** injects the correct `User-Agent` and a stable synthetic `x-opencode-session` / `x-opencode-session-id` pair per client, then re-exposes everything as a plain OpenAI API. No accounts, no API keys, no source patches.

> works with: **mimo cli**, **Cline**, **Roo Code**, **Continue**, **Aider**, opencode forks — anything that lets you set a `baseURL` + `apiKey`.

  ▸ feature list
  
    - **OpenAI-compatible API** — `/v1/chat/completions` (stream + non-stream), `/v1/models`, `/v1/responses`
    - **UA unlock** — injects `User-Agent: opencode/1.18.30` plus a stable per-client `x-opencode-session` / `x-opencode-session-id` pair upstream, the things that open the free tier
    - **BYOK** — ride anonymous `public` or bring your own Zen key (stable + no shared-pool throttling)
    - **Smart fallback** — tries models in order on `429`/`5xx` and dead-model `4xx` (e.g. "Model is unavailable"), honors `retry-after`
    - **Model aliases** — e.g. `gpt-4o → mimo-v2.5-free`, replies rewritten back
    - **Per-IP fairness** — real client IPs forwarded; local clients fall back to the machine's real IP
    - **Management dashboard** — glass… no, sticker-style UI at `/` for stats, model tests, config & logs
    - **Zero dependencies** — one `zen-proxy.mjs`, runs on any Node ≥ 18
  

---

## install

Requires **Node.js ≥ 18**.

**Linux / macOS**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/12errh/zen-proxy/main/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/12errh/zen-proxy/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

Or just clone and run — it's a single file, no `npm install`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/12errh/zen-proxy.git && cd zen-proxy
node zen-proxy.mjs
```

---

## usage

```bash
node zen-proxy.mjs            # or the installer's `zen-proxy` launcher
# dashboard → http://127.0.0.1:8787/
```

| Thing | Value |
|---|---|
| Dashboard / admin UI | `http://127.0.0.1:8787/` |
| OpenAI base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1` |
| API key | `public` (any value once you set `proxyKey`) |
| Example model | `mimo-v2.5-free` (auto default picks a healthy free model) |
| Health check | `http://127.0.0.1:8787/health` |

### point your agent at it

Cline / Roo / Continue / Aider / mimo — anywhere you configure an OpenAI-compatible provider:

```jsonc
{
  "provider": {
    "zen": {
      "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1",
      "apiKey": "public",
      "models": { "mimo-v2.5-free": {} }
    }
  }
}
```

Quick test:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"mimo-v2.5-free","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}]}'
```

---

## the dashboard

manage everything, no config files

- **Overview** — upstream health, uptime, request counters, live recent-request feed with status + latency
- **Models** — add/remove allowed models, pick the default, one-click **Test** per model
- **Settings** — edit host, port, upstream URL, User-Agent, proxy key, BYOK key, timeout, fallback list, aliases; saved to `zen-proxy.json` and applied instantly
- **Logs** — live terminal-style log tail

Set `proxyKey` and both the dashboard and the API require that key.

---

## Claude Code quick start

One command, on Linux, macOS and Windows alike:

```bash
zen-claude
```

It starts zen-proxy if it is not already running, waits for it to answer, registers every live free Zen model in Claude Code's `/model` picker, launches Claude Code against them, and stops the proxy again on exit. It deliberately does not `exec claude`; if it did, its exit trap would never fire and the auto-started proxy would be left running. `zen-claude "fix the failing test"` works too. If Claude Code is not installed it says so and prints the install command.

`bin/claude-zen` (bash) and `bin/claude-zen.ps1` (PowerShell, invoked through `claude-zen.cmd`) implement the same flow. Note the command is `zen-claude` while the script is `bin/claude-zen`; the installer links **both** names on posix (`~/.local/bin`) and copies both `.cmd` shims on Windows (`%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`), adding that directory to the user PATH. Linking only the script's own basename was a real bug that shipped: it installed `claude-zen`, so `zen-claude` reported `command not found` after an otherwise successful install. There is now a test asserting the installer links the name the docs use.

Both use `--settings` rather than exported environment variables, because Claude Code reads env from `~/.claude/settings.json` and that takes precedence over the shell — so exporting `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is silently ignored if that file already sets it. Existing Claude Code configuration is left alone; a plain `claude` still uses it.

`bin/make-settings.mjs` generates the settings: it reads the live model list from the proxy's `/v1/models` (falling back to `models.json`) and writes one `modelPicker` row per free model, each with `behavesAs` set to a model this Claude Code version already knows. `replaceBuiltInOptions` hides Claude Code's own lineup, whose models the proxy cannot serve.

If `zen-claude` reports `command not found`, check the symlink exists before blaming PATH: `ls -l ~/.local/bin/zen-claude`. If it is missing, re-run the installer — an older one linked only `claude-zen`. If it exists but the shell cannot see it, the shell's PATH predates the install: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`. The installer verifies both `zen-proxy` and `zen-claude` resolve and prints the exact fix when they do not.

---

## Anthropic API (Claude Code)

`POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` implement the Anthropic Messages protocol: system blocks, message content blocks, images, `tool_use`/`tool_result`, `thinking`, `tool_choice` and `stop_sequences` are all translated to the endpoint family the target model actually uses, and the reply is translated back including the full streaming envelope (`message_start` → `content_block_*` → `message_delta` → `message_stop`). Errors use Anthropic's `{type:"error",error:{type,message}}` shape. Both `x-api-key` and `Authorization: Bearer` authenticate.

The free tier accepts an Anthropic request only when it also carries opencode's own tool manifest. Claude Code's system prompt is passed through untouched — it is never edited or replaced — but the proxy attaches opencode's built-in tools next to the caller's, limited to those the caller has a counterpart for, and renames resulting calls (`read`→`Read`, `filePath`→`file_path`, …) so the caller runs the tool it knows. Disable with `agentTools: false`.

The same gate applies to callers that bring **only their own tools** and pin one with `tool_choice` (`{"type":"tool","name":…}`): the gate wants a tool literally named `read`, and a helper like `set_title` matches nothing, so the proxy adds a stub `read` riding along whenever a pinned request's list lacks one — and a pinned reply is filtered back down to the pinned call, streaming included (a stray call's argument chunks are dropped with it, because a call's name arrives chunks apart from its arguments). When every call got filtered away the reply ends `end_turn`/`stop` instead of claiming a tool call that does not exist. Unpinned replies are never filtered.

## Responses API

`POST /v1/responses` reads either dialect, decided by the body, and answers in the same one: a body that speaks Responses (`input`, flat tools, `tool_choice: {"type":"function","name":…}`, `max_output_tokens`, optional `instructions`) is translated — on chat-family models via chat completions, and reply items are rebuilt in Responses shape (`message` items with `output_text`, `function_call` items, `reasoning`); a chat-shaped `messages` body is answered with a `chat.completion` as before. Streaming emits the gateway's own Responses SSE (`response.created` → `output_item.added` / `output_text.delta` / `function_call_arguments.delta` → `response.completed`, no `[DONE]`); on responses-family models the upstream stream passes through with the model id rewritten. The free-tier bridge and pinned-call rules apply here identically: a tool-less body gets opencode's manifest and every manifest call is stripped from the reply, and a pinned request keeps only the pinned call. Reasoning items in the request are skipped (their provider state has no chat counterpart).

## configuration

Config lives in **`zen-proxy.json`** (auto-created on first run, hot-reloaded when edited — the dashboard writes it too). Env vars can override at startup.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `host` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address (restart needed) |
| `port` | `8787` | Listen port (restart needed) |
| `upstream` | `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1` | Zen API base |
| `ua` | `opencode/1.18.30` | The `User-Agent` that unlocks the free tier (auto-updates to new opencode releases) |
| `autoUA` | `true` | Track opencode releases and update `ua` automatically (`opencode/<latest>`) |
| `uaRefreshMs` | `21600000` | How often to check for a new opencode version (ms) |
| `injectSession` | `true` | Mint the `x-opencode-session` + `x-opencode-session-id` pair per client (upstream rejects requests that lack either) |
| `gated` (sync state) | — | Models answering `403 FreeTierError`: the free tier only accepts genuine agent requests, so our probe can't verify them. Shown as **agent-only**, kept in the list, never removed |
| `probeAuth` | `auto` | Credentials for auto-sync health probes: `auto` (your Zen key if set, else anonymous), `anonymous` (always the public free tier), or `key` (always your key, so probes reflect your own quota) |
| `defaultModel` | `""` | Empty = auto: pick the first *healthy* free model (no more hardcoded/vanished defaults) |
| `fallbackModels` | *(from `models.json`)* | Tried in order on `429`/`5xx` and dead-model `4xx`. Omit it to follow the shipped catalog (refreshed by the model-sync Action every 6h); save it from the dashboard to pin your own list |
| `responsesModels` | `["gpt-5*","gpt-6*","grok-*","muse-spark-*"]` | Models served on `/v1/responses` (patterns may end in `*`); the proxy translates to/from chat completions for you |
| `rateLimitMax` | `0` (off) | Max chat requests per client per window — `0` disables the limiter |
| `rateLimitWindowMs` | `60000` | Rate-limit window |
| `modelAliases` | `{}` | e.g. `{"gpt-4o":"mimo-v2.5-free"}` — reply model rewritten back |
| `proxyKey` | `""` | If set, clients must send it as `Bearer`; locks the dashboard too |
| `defaultZenKey` | `""` | Your own Zen key (BYOK) instead of anonymous `public` |
| `trustForwarded` | `false` | Trust `x-forwarded-for`/`x-real-ip` from a reverse proxy |
| `timeoutMs` | `120000` | Upstream timeout for non-streaming |
| `cacheMs` | `30000` | `/v1/models` cache TTL |

Env vars: `HOST`, `PORT`, `ZEN_URL`, `ZEN_UA`, `INJECT_SESSION` (`0` to disable), `AUTO_UA` (`0` to disable), `UA_REFRESH_MS`, `PROBE_AUTH`, `RESPONSES_MODELS` (JSON), `RATE_LIMIT_MAX`, `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`, `DEFAULT_MODEL`, `FALLBACK_MODELS` (JSON), `MODEL_ALIASES` (JSON), `PROXY_KEY`, `ZEN_KEY`, `TRUST_FORWARDED=1`, `TIMEOUT_MS`, `CACHE_MS`, `ZEN_PROXY_CONFIG` (custom config path).

### bring your own key

Anonymous `public` access rides opencode's shared free pool (per-IP quota, sometimes saturated). For stable, reliable use set `defaultZenKey` to your own free Zen key — or send it per request as `x-zen-key` / a non-`public` bearer token.

---

## api surface

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` | Chat completions (stream + non-stream) |
| `POST` | `/v1/responses` | Responses API in either dialect — Responses bodies on the route get Responses replies, chat bodies keep chat replies; bridge and pinned filters apply |
| `GET` | `/v1/models` | Allowed models (cached) |
| `GET` | `/health` | Health check |
| `GET` | `/` | Dashboard |
| `GET` | `/api/status` | Stats + upstream health |
| `GET/PUT` | `/api/config` | Read / update config |
| `POST` | `/api/test` | Test a model (`{"model":"…"}`) |
| `GET` | `/api/logs` | Log tail |
| `POST` | `/api/reset` | Reset request stats |
| `GET` | `/assets/*` | Static assets (logo, favicon) |

---

## systemd (linux)

Install as a service via `install.sh` (it prompts you), or manually:

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now zen-proxy
```

---

## the free-tier gate (read this if a model says "agent-only")

opencode serves its free models **only to genuine opencode traffic**. Verified by capturing and replaying a real opencode request, the upstream accepts a request only when it carries:

- a valid session pair (`x-opencode-session` **and** `x-opencode-session-id`), **and**
- `stream: true`, **and**
- a system message carrying opencode's **own** wording (roughly its first 1 kB)

Body size is irrelevant: a realistic 1.5 kB agent prompt of our own wording is refused, and `'x' * 2000` is refused too. Only opencode's actual prompt text passes, so no synthetic probe can verify a free model — a retired model is refused with exactly the same 403, so probing cannot tell the two apart either. Which free models *exist* comes from opencode's public `/models` catalog instead, via `models.json`.

A bare `curl`, a health probe, or any non-agent client gets:

```
403 FreeTierError: OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode
```

**This is not the model being broken.** A model in this state is shown as **agent-only**, is kept in your list, and is never pruned. Because the built-in probe can't verify it, the proxy learns real health from your actual client traffic — a model that serves your agent shows **`ok (live traffic)`**.

| badge | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok (live traffic)` | a real request through the proxy succeeded — the strongest signal |
| `agent-only` | the synthetic probe was gated; unproven either way, kept in your list |
| `flaky` | temporary trouble (timeout, 5xx, rate-limit) |
| `dead` | upstream no longer lists the model in `/models` — the only state that removes it |

### Does my agent need anything?

If your agent **streams** (Claude Code, Cline, Roo Code, Continue, Aider, mimo, opencode itself — all of them do), it works. A one-shot non-streaming client gets gated on those calls, and the proxy transparently falls back to another free model.

You don't need to change anything. When a fallback happens the response tells you:

```jsonc
{ "model": "mimo-v2.6-flash-free", "zen_served_by": "space-bunny-free", /* … */ }
```

plus response headers `x-zen-served-by` and `x-zen-fallback: true`.

> The proxy deliberately does **not** fake opencode's tool schemas to get past this check. That gate is an access control, and the honest behaviour is to tell you which models are gated and let your real agent traffic use them.

---

## caveats

- This rides opencode's **anonymous free tier**: per-IP request/daily quotas and a shared pool that's sometimes saturated. Don't rotate/abuse IPs or run heavy workloads anonymously.
- opencode keeps **tightening the anonymous free tier** — most `-free` models now answer `403 FreeTierError: "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"`, and that hits the real opencode client too. The proxy detects it and rolls to the next working model, so requests keep succeeding, but the pool is much smaller than it used to be. A Zen API key (BYOK) is the reliable path.
- The `-free` models are "as-is" free tiers — expect rate limits and occasional provider errors.
- For anything serious, **BYOK**.
